properties.name: gap_to_prompt requires the whole gap OBJECT and reads only its id, so its consumer re-runs detect_gaps on every click to rebuild something the server discards
properties.statement:
FLO2 F22. The tool's own description is honest — 'THE REPLAYED GAP IS AN ECHO: only its `id` is read, and the server resolves the gap afresh' — and the shape contradicts it.

MEASURED 2026-09-19 on the committed toolsnap: `required: ['gap']`, `gap` is of type `object`, and the PARAMETER's own description reads in full 'A `GapCandidate` previously returned by `detect_gaps`.' The echo caveat lives on the TOOL's description, not on the parameter, so a caller reading the parameter meets an object and no hint that a key would do.

flo2 believed the shape, which is the right instinct: A PARAMETER'S TYPE IS LOUDER THAN ITS PROSE. Its `gapPrompt()` therefore re-runs detect_gaps on EVERY send to rebuild an object the server immediately throws away and re-resolves — a whole graph computation per click, for nothing.

⭐ AND THE REPORTER FOUND THE BETTER FIX WHILE COMPLAINING: their redundant call is also how a stale chip gets refused with 'that is no longer open'. If gap_to_prompt answered a vanished gap with a DISTINGUISHABLE refusal, flo2 could drop the extra call entirely and still be correct — which closes the cost and the correctness question together, where taking an id alone closes only the first.
